timeline.label: Groundwork starts
timeline.description: Rights and Resources Initiative begins consultations on a financial mechanism to support tenure rights.

timeline.label: Independent NGO
timeline.description: Tenure Facility is formally founded as an independent NGO.

timeline.label: First grant
timeline.description: First grant is awarded and work expands to three new countries.

timeline.label: Breakthrough
timeline.description: 13 projects with US$5M grants; Tenure Facility becomes a TED Audacious grantee.

timeline.label: Gathering pace
timeline.description: 14 projects with US$12M grants and ROOTS framework operational.

timeline.label: Accelerating steadily
timeline.description: 29 projects with US$26M grants; strategic framework launched to secure 60M ha by 2027.

timeline.label: Advisory Group reformed
timeline.description: Tenure Facility launched a reformed 20-member Advisory Group to provide independent strategic guidance across regions and generations.

timeline.label: Board transitions led by Indigenous women
timeline.description: Three new Indigenous women joined the Board in 2024, with Joan Carling appointed Chair and Carl Lindgren as Vice-Chair.

timeline.label: Funding base broadened
timeline.description: The 2024 budget (just under USD 40 million) was supported by two dozen funders, including three new funders.

timeline.label: Momentum builds
timeline.description: 35 projects active and US$30M disbursed; UK invests up to GBP 94M in the Amazon Catalyst.

timeline.label: Operational systems strengthened
timeline.description: 2024 improvements included ROOTS project-management consolidation, simplified results reporting, updated procurement policy, and IT incident response training.

timeline.label: Team footprint expanded
timeline.description: By end-2024, team presence reached 56 staff: 25 in Stockholm and 31 in other locations, mostly in project regions.

timeline.label: Trust-based funding model articulated
timeline.description: Part Three codifies a fit-for-purpose, rights-based funding model centered on partner trust, flexible finance, and long-term capacity support.

glossary.definition: A 20-member independent group launched in 2024 to provide high-level strategic guidance, challenge assumptions, and strengthen global-local alignment.
A rights-based financing approach that tailors support to partner capacity, combines flexible long-term funding with compliance support, and centers community self-determination.

A multi-pronged strategy through which communities strengthen and sustain rights to traditional lands, territories, and resources, including mapping, conflict resolution, governance strengthening, and defence against external threats.
Financial mechanisms managed by grassroots organisations representing communities to finance long-term land, governance, and livelihood priorities.
Community-led systems, institutions, and decision-making structures used to manage lands, forests, waters, and resources according to collective rights and priorities.

methodology.summary: Figures and stories are extracted from the Tenure Facility Annual Report 2024. Country boundaries are sourced from authoritative TopoJSON in the project geo manifest, while project territory overlays remain supplemental GeoJSON prepared outside the PDF for digital storytelling and exploration.

about.vision: Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendant Peoples, and local communities thrive in their ancestral territories with full recognition of their right to own, manage, and develop their traditional lands, territories, and resources.
about.mission: To work in partnership with Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendant Peoples, and local communities to strengthen their tenure and ability to preserve, protect, and enjoy the benefits of their traditional lands, territories, and resources.

values.name: Respect
values.description: For Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendant Peoples, and local communities; for the team and stakeholders; and for the planet.

values.name: Reliability
values.description: A culture of accountability, transparency, equity, and timeliness.

values.name: Trust
values.description: Nurturing trusting, responsible, and longstanding relationships with communities and stakeholders.

pillars.title: Source
pillars.description: Supporting Indigenous Peoples, Afro-descendant Peoples and local community-led initiatives rooted in their traditions and priorities, with assistance tailored to local needs for scalable systemic change.

pillars.title: Secure
pillars.description: Achieving recognition of land and forest rights through legal and administrative processes, participatory mapping, and conflict resolution, with inclusive decision-making for women and youth.

pillars.title: Sustain
pillars.description: Strengthening social cohesion, cultural identities, organisational capacity, territorial monitoring, traditional knowledge, and local economic development to defend land and forest rights.

pillars.title: Share
pillars.description: Facilitating knowledge exchange and advocacy to amplify success, influence policy narratives, and mobilise additional resources to scale impact.
